name: Klausism
summary: The political outlook of Václav Klaus, founder of the Czech Civic Democratic Party: radical free-market liberalisation, privatisation and a small state, combined with defence of the nation state against European integration, hostility to environmentalism and climate policy, opposition to mass migration and multiculturalism, and cultural conservatism on family and gender. Klaus presents it as classical liberalism in economics and conservatism in culture, against what he calls Europeism and the post-democratic 'isms'.
scope: Klaus's own articulated doctrine, 1989-2026: his speeches and essays on klaus.cz (Europeism, transition, climate, migration, the nation state) and Prushankin's scholarly analysis of his early texts. Excludes other ODS platforms, 'Klausism without Klaus' politicians, and the practice of his governments, which ruled in coalition and compromised (retained welfare, rent caps); only his stated positions are used.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He describes communism as an experiment that cancelled private ownership and paralysed money.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: He objects to the 'de-assimilation principle' and says countries need a minimum degree of homogeneity.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: He says governments should not try to produce growth by stimuli and should cut spending, and that belief in macro-control was the wrong 'Great Moderation' dogma.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: He wants parties with defined ideologies rather than civic movements or NGOs, and criticises bypassing parliamentary politics.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He says the market brings infinitely better results than any alternative and that his generation wanted capitalism as the 'first way'.

central-planning.rationale: He treats centrally administered economies as the tragic episode of communism and says only markets handle shortages through prices.

common-currency.rationale: He calls the euro a failed system for a non-optimal area and wants countries free to leave it.

corporate-influence.rationale: He says powerful business lobby groups suppress market adjustment and lobby for cheap imported labour.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: He rejects corporatism, social partnership and Galbraithian countervailing powers of big business and big unions.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: He says the generous European welfare state must be stopped and that welfare lets people leave the labour force.

decide-locally.rationale: He lists the shift of power from local and regional authorities to central ones as a harm and wants decentralisation, while defending the nation state as the base unit.

defend-planned-state.rationale: He wanted capitalism and free markets and fought the planned economy, and sees no case for defending it.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He defends classical parliamentary democracy and says the transition produced democracy but not classical liberalism, treating the two as separable.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: He defends 'good old political politics' against post-democracy and wants ideologically defined parties, not civic movements.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He rejects communist rule as totalitarian and part of the tragic communist episode.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He says countries need a minimum of homogeneity and that mass migration necessarily brings cultural and social conflict.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He calls fighting the climate one of the greatest mistakes of our time and rejects radical measures.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He rejects collectivism and says the individual is the basic unit of democracy.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He favours removing border barriers and condemns protectionism, which contradicts an autarkic bloc shut off from trade.

elite-replacement.rationale: He says European elites organise mass migration as an ethnic restructuring project that erodes homogeneous nations.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He rejects global governance and supranational organisations and says democracy needs a demos at the nation-state level.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He argues NATO is here to stay and that its role in Europe stays important.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: His thesis is that freedom, not the climate, is endangered and that environmentalism limits liberty.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He calls the European system excessively redistributing and defends the market as unfeeling about winners and losers.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He wants 'basically monocultural' nation states and objects to the erosion of 'more or less homogenous' European nations.

experts-over-public.rationale: He rejects governance by experts and intellectuals chosen without democratic accountability and says Europeists trust 'the chosen ones, not the elected ones'.

farm-price-support.rationale: He likens the Common Agricultural Policy to central planning with price manipulation and subsidy dependence, and earlier told farmers the market admits no exceptions.

free-trade.rationale: He says the only effective way to help poor countries is to trade freely with them without quotas, limits or barriers, and praises removing barriers to exchange.

future-generations.rationale: He argues future losses should be discounted so that present generations need not worry, and rejects the aim of an unspoiled original Earth.

gender-social-construct.rationale: He counts genderism among the main threats and says it questions the natural sexual orientation of men and women.

government-nudges.rationale: He rejects paternalism and the idea that people must be guided by those who know what is good for them.

gradual-change.rationale: He prizes spontaneous evolution and proven institutions, yet urged rapid, 'merciless' transition rather than half-measures.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: He argues the mild warming is not dominantly man-made or CO2-made and calls carbon dioxide a minor player.

individual-rights-only.rationale: He criticises Europeists for preferring collectivity and collective rights to the individual and individual rights.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He champions technical progress, markets and prosperity and calls environmentalism anti-human.

islam-incompatible.rationale: He says Islam is respectable and no threat where it stays, yet condemns its being imported into Europe; his remarks point both ways.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Asked directly, he says the right-left dispute is here and will stay.

limit-growth.rationale: He holds that adaptation, markets and growth deal with climate and that mitigation means a world-wide economic decline.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Klaus holds that government failure is far bigger than market failure and that the market is the best, fairest and most democratic mechanism of human interaction.

national-law-over-international.rationale: He objects to supranational legal bodies and EU law overriding the sovereignty of states and their parliaments.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: He rejects the environmentalist starting point of Earth or Nature rather than Man and calls it anti-human.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He says there are only two ways, that a 'third way' is a fatal conceit and that after communism the aim was the first way, capitalism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He says the Europeist belief in government as productive above the minimal classic-liberal concept is the error, but he also stresses a strong rules-based order.

no-bailouts.rationale: He wants Europeans to say NO to bailouts, says some states must be left to fall, and mocks costly rescue packages.

no-business-privileges.rationale: He wants Europe to desubsidise and attacks business lobbies and subsidised firms that profit from government schemes.

one-party-rule.rationale: He calls communism a tragic episode and defends competitive parliamentary party politics.

open-borders.rationale: He calls closing EU borders a necessity and removing borders a utopian ambition.

party-controls-media.rationale: He condemns authoritarianism in ideas and the suppression of free exchange of views, citing life under communism.

person-over-state.rationale: Cited in Prushankin, Klaus holds that individualism means the state must serve the person and be controlled by him.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He calls elites detached, self-interested and arrogant, says people-versus-elite is today's fundamental issue, but does not say corrupt in general.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He opposes supranational unification, wants a return to intergovernmentalism and calls the EU in its current form a tragic mistake.

precautionary-principle.rationale: He asks for 'rational risk-aversion instead of reliance on the precautionary principle'.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He says mass migration destabilises nations, their culture and traditions, and that Europeism erodes the nation state.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: He called for 'merciless' price liberalisation and treats price manipulation as a feature of planned economies.

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: He called for 'merciless' price liberalisation and holds prices should adjust to fix shortages.

public-ownership.rationale: His programme was fast privatisation to 'real private owners' and an end to bureaucrats' control of enterprises; the sources record no case for public ownership of utilities.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He wants mass migration, legal and illegal, stopped and says Europe needs none of it.

regulate-corporations.rationale: His slogan is 'deregulate, liberalize, privatize'; he holds regulation is a weapon of interest groups and that the 2008 crisis was a government failure, not a market one.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He says foreign aid mostly wastes money and helps corrupt governments, and endorses the view that duty is owed first to fellow citizens.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He lists registered partnerships and same-sex marriage among the ways Europeism undermines the family.

self-interest-moral.rationale: He fears ideas that following private interest is wrong and that public interest must dominate.

social-market-economy.rationale: He calls the social market economy the opposite of a market economy and demands 'markets without adjectives'; he wants Europe to get rid of it.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Klaus holds government is never competent to substitute for micro-level decisions of firms and individuals and rejects government 'masterminding' of the economy.

state-harmful.rationale: He calls the nation state an unsubstitutable guarantor of democracy and rejects 'unnecessary' as a description of it.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He argues NATO is here to stay, backs Czech entry and says transatlantic cooperation should continue.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He insists that free debate and opposition are the core of democracy and attacks efforts to silence critics.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He wants protectionism ended and counts 'getting rid of protectionism' among integration's successes.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: He tells Europe to cut government spending and forget solutions based on tax increases; he says nothing on wealthy taxpayers in particular.

total-state.rationale: He calls for decentralising, deregulating and desubsidising and condemns central administration of society.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He speaks of Communist and Nazi totalitarian regimes together and calls fascist variants 'not less evil'.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: He wants free trade with poor countries 'without imposing social, environmental and other standards'.

traditional-family.rationale: He names the family as one of the traditional building blocks of European society that Europeism undermines.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: He endorses the view that duty is owed first to fellow citizens and wants the welfare state that draws migrants stopped.

women-suffrage.rationale: He says equal rights for women have to be guaranteed while criticising feminism.

work-for-welfare.rationale: He criticises systems that give people money from sources other than actual work and claim there is no obligation to work.

missingStatements.text: Genuine democracy is possible only at the level of the nation state.
missingStatements.rationale: Klaus repeatedly holds that democracy needs a demos and that only the nation state can supply one.

quotes.text: It is the nation state which is the exclusive and irreplaceable playing field of democracy, and its only guarantor.
We can't have democracy at the level of the European Union, with 27 different nation states.
Europe should return to democracy which can exist only at the level of nation-states, not at the level of the whole continent.

missingStatements.text: The European Union should not harmonise the laws of its member states.
missingStatements.rationale: Klaus backs the original liberalising model of integration and opposes unification through harmonisation.

quotes.text: the removal of all unnecessary barriers to human activities existing on the borders of states
quotes.where: section 2, the model of the integration process

quotes.text: Europe should get rid of the excessive centralization, harmonization, standardization of the continent

missingStatements.text: Disputes over climate policy are mainly disputes about political values.
missingStatements.rationale: Klaus argues the global warming debate is an ideological clash over freedom and markets, not a scientific one.

quotes.text: It is an ideological clash between those who want to change us (rather than the climate) and those who believe in freedom, markets, human ingenuity, and technical progress.
is in its substance not part of the scientific discourse

missingStatements.declined: A claim about the nature of a debate, not a position.

notes: Based on 16 sources, mostly Klaus's own English-language speeches. Themes searched: economy and welfare, tax and spending, trade and aid, EU integration and the euro, nation state, democracy, migration and multiculturalism, family and gender, climate and environment, NATO and geopolitics, communism. Searched without finding a position: healthcare, minimum wage, unions, drugs, abortion, death penalty, policing, courts, voting systems, religion and state, race, animals, technology (nuclear, AI). Klaus's 2026 Oxford speech says it is wrong to fight communism now, which sits against his earlier anti-communism, so defeat-communism is left null. Klaus's governments (coalition, 1992-97) kept social protection; this is not treated as the ideology's record. Climate claims are Klaus's political position, not a scientific finding.

keyFigures.role: Founder of the Civic Democratic Party, Czech prime minister 1992-97 and president 2003-13; the doctrine's originator and namesake.
